displayName.description: CdoId: 1000; FieldId: 6184; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element.  For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object.   The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character.   This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used.  DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

aceMessage.description:
CdoId: 1100; FieldId: 10971; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ACEMessage field contains the success or failure messages of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitFailure)
On unhandled errors in these events, System automatically populates this field with the resolved error message.

aceStatus.description:
CdoId: 1100; FieldId: 10972; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure)
Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.

Value	Name	                Meaning
1	ACESuccess	after commit event completed successfully
2	ACEFSuccess	an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully
3	ACEFFail	                an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event
> 99	<custom status>	User specific status codes (Designer based)

isExternalAppTxnExecution.description: CdoId: 1110; FieldId: 28378; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: The flag indicates whether a transaction was initiated by an external application, such as through a REST API call. This field is crucial for managing data broadcasts, like controlling a SignalR broadcast. By default, the flag is set to false, allowing normal broadcasting of data. However, when the flag is set to true, it serves as a control mechanism to prevent broadcasting the transaction data. This indicates that the transaction was executed externally, and therefore, should not be broadcast back.
